challenges.says: The why says typing mistakes never silently change a value, but the cited rule clamps a too-large hexadecimal number to the largest allowed value without any message, and the what adds "decimal or marked hexadecimal" that no cited rule states.
The sixth criterion says "the three policy branches of the registry" without naming them, so a product owner who never saw the code cannot tell which values are forgotten.
The story and its criterion use "semantic policy text" and "the fragment" without explaining either, which a person who never saw the code could not follow.

The last criterion adds that the screens receive each policy state "as plain facts", which the cited rule does not say and a product owner cannot follow; the criteria also lean on undefined words such as "element" and "switched-on effects".
